note: P4360 (Pro 30:2) — surely I am too stupid to be a man; I have not a man's understanding. (Agur's confession.)

dims.v: humble self-abasement — Agur owning himself too stupid to be a man
the confession of Agur that he is too stupid/brutish to be a man — the profound humility that, before God's wisdom, owns its own ignorance, the ground on which true wisdom begins
welded to the human understanding he confesses to lack

baar (be brutish/stupid) — 'surely I am too STUPID to be a man'; Agur opens by confessing his own ignorance. Such humility is not despair but the beginning of wisdom — the wise know how little they know (cf 30:3; 26:12; Job 42:3).
owned ignorance — Agur disclaiming a man's understanding before God
the understanding that Agur confesses he does not have — the honest disclaiming of his own wisdom before the knowledge of the Holy One, humility that makes room for God to teach
the confessed brutishness it belongs with (267164)
welded to the self-abasement that owns it

binah (understanding) — 'I have not the UNDERSTANDING of a man'; Agur owns that he lacks true understanding, disclaiming wisdom before God (30:3-4). To confess ignorance before the Holy One is the humility on which real knowledge is built.
